title: Noise Amplification for Non-Uniform Secrets
summary: Existing noisy-leakage amplification lemmas require mutually independent, uniformly distributed shares; proving amplification with non-uniform secrets remains open.

formal_statement.body: Prove a noise-amplification theorem for masked computations in the noisy leakage model when the secret is non-uniform, extending beyond existing amplification lemmata that assume mutually independent, uniformly distributed shares; the theorem should establish noise amplification under the non-uniform-secret setting itself.

scope.domain: Masked computations and noise amplification in the noisy leakage model.
scope.unresolved_remainder: Establish noise amplification for masked computations with a non-uniform secret, beyond lemmas restricted to mutually independent, uniformly distributed shares.

citations.label: Prou? & Rivain’s Formal Security Proof of Masking, Revisited: Tight Bounds in the Noisy Leakage Model

progress.summary: The source reports that existing amplification lemmas for direct noisy-leakage proofs require mutually independent, uniformly distributed shares. It explicitly identifies amplification for non-uniform secrets as an open challenge.
citation_labels: Loïc Masure et al., Prou? & Rivain’s Formal Security Proof of Masking, Revisited: Tight Bounds in the Noisy Leakage Model
